title: Bun 1.4 Rewrote the Core From Zig to Rust
caption:
Bun shipped its biggest release yet and almost none of it is something you can actually use.

At the v1.3.0 tag the repo built with build.zig and src/bun.zig. At v1.4.0, published August 20, both are gone — src is a Cargo workspace with 100 crates.

What landed for me as a user: bun prune, bun dedupe, bun test --parallel, XML imports. Four new pages in the docs.

Honestly I respect it. Nobody gets applause for a rewrite that changes nothing on the surface.

Would you rewrite it?

slides.headline:
Bun rewrote itself
in Rust.
slides.sub: Bun 1.4 shipped August 20. build.zig is gone from the repo and src is now a Cargo workspace.

slides.title: 100 crates, one binary
slides.sub: Cargo.toml at the v1.4.0 tag lists 100 workspace members: parser, bundler, installer, HTTP, SQL, each its own crate.

slides.title: What you actually get
items: bun prune deletes what bun.lock would not install, without touching the registry
bun dedupe collapses duplicate versions in bun.lock onto one
bun test --parallel spreads test files across CPU cores
Bun.XML.parse, plus importing .xml files, marked New in Bun v1.4
